title: Assume only what was taught and kept
statement: A lesson may assume only what earlier lessons taught and the learner still holds fluently, so record what each lesson assumes and adds, and check the whole sequence in code.
detail: The reading project's instruction spec makes it a code-checked invariant that a lesson assumes only what earlier lessons taught, and counts an anchor as available only after a delayed ≥24h retest passed on new parallel items, so one first taught the same day, or present but not fluent, is not met (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/instruction-modes-spec.md`, section 4). A committed negative fixture, a lesson assuming knowledge no earlier lesson added, was scored as individually fine by the per-lesson quality evaluator and was caught only by the cross-lesson invariant (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/handoffs-2026-07-13/course-eval-layer/evaluator-spec.md`). The course standard asks that each prerequisite be established, activated, retaught, newly introduced or routed through a tested on-ramp (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q015); the curriculum BrainLift says a prerequisite that is met but not automated enough to free working memory makes the target skill unteachable (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback1/Curriculum & Knowledge BrainLift.md`), and the project's curriculum reference gives soft prerequisites a fluency threshold rather than a binary met or unmet (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/train-teacher/references/curriculum-architecture.md`). Fluently here means well enough on a later day to leave working memory free. To hold a course to this, record what each lesson builds on and seeds, keep every keystone later lessons need, and check the whole sequence in code, failing any lesson the check can't find.
against: The same spec says the code check supplements, never replaces, human sequence review (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/instruction-modes-spec.md`, lines 59-60). The check runs only within a unit and has no baseline across units, so a unit's first lesson must assume nothing (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/scripts/lane-tools/op-lint/README.md`, lines 67-68). These are the doctrine's positions, with worked examples, not results measured here. The check supplements, never replaces, a person's review of the sequence (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/instruction-modes-spec.md`), and the record of what each text introduces is still proposed (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/handoffs-2026-07-13/course-eval-layer/evaluator-spec.md`). The drop was disclosed as a deliberate design choice: the later grade's lessons were written to stand alone rather than build on the grade before (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/CURRICULUM-REVIEW-STANDING-2026-08-17.md`, line 70).
